page.overview:
What is Simpson family?

The Simpson family is the titular protagonist of The Simpsons franchise. They are a middle-class American family based in Springfield and its tri-city area.

Though not a hugely wealthy family, multiple members had confronted Springfield's most powerful man and Homer Simpson's boss, Charles Montgomery Burns, (though Burns also respected Abraham "Grampa" Simpson in his role as 1950s heel wrestler Glamorous Godfrey), and had a significant impact, both on Mr. Burns's life and elsewhere. Homer Simpson have had success as a musician when he was younger, was a talent agent, and a successful talk show host, had caused massive environmental crises from neglect, and financially ruined his half-brother Herb Powell's automobile company Powell Motors and the Groovy Grove Juice Corporation. Bart Simpson was a child star, and Bart and Lisa had written popular cartoons. According to Homer, "The Simpson family is a long line of horse thieves, deadbeats, horse beats, dead thieves, and even a few alcoholics."

Throughout the family, there are two traditions that have been passed on. The first is the way they handle their fights, fighting dirty and attacking the opponent in their "family jewels". The second is how they treat their children, preferring to strangle as a form of punishment. Orville Simpson had strangled his son Abraham Simpson II to show how to punish a child for his parenting classes, which resulted in his father "Old Tut" Simpson strangling Orville as a punishment, implying that "Old Tut" had punished Orville as a child by strangling him. It is possible that this started with Virgil Simpson, who was an abused slave owner by Wainwright Montgomery Burns, who could've strangled his slaves as punishment.

The Simpson family are also distant relatives of the Van Houten family, since Eliza Simpson had married Milford Van Houten, the ancestor of the Van Houtens.
